notes: Frequency: 4 gym sessions/week (two upper, two lower) + 1 optional easy conditioning/recovery day
Progression: conservative over 3 weeks; auto-regulation using RPE/RIR
Volume: 2–4 working sets for heavy lifts, moderate assistance volume
Tempo: controlled eccentrics (2–3s) and full range; pause reps where helpful
Warm-up: 8–12 minutes general (bike/row), joint mobility, 2–3 ramp sets before heavy work
Cool-down: 5–10 minutes light cardio, foam rolling and breathing practice
Rest & recovery: aim for 8–9 hours sleep where possible
Nutrition plan: mild calorie surplus (250–500 kcal/day) to regain ~0.5–1 kg/week first 2 weeks; protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day spread across meals
Hydration & electrolytes (especially sodium) recommended
Monitoring: check resting HR and subjective energy/fatigue daily; reduce intensity/volume if resting HR >8–10 bpm above baseline or worsening fatigue
Week 1 focus: re-intro, technique, low-moderate intensity, conservative volume
Week 2 focus: build intensity to ~70–80%, slightly increase sets; begin heavier singles/doubles on day 3 if recovered
Week 3 focus: peak toward previous loads (~80–90%) if recovered; keep total volume lower than pre-illness
Session structure examples: Upper A, Lower A, Upper B, Lower B
Optional Day 5 active recovery: 30–45 min brisk walk, light bike, mobility and breathing work
If energy is good, add a single heavy double or single on deadlift at RPE 7–8 in week 2
If persistent fatigue or weight still low in week 3, reduce top intensities to ~75% and keep reps higher
Do not push to true PRs in this block; reassess at end of week 3 before 1–3RM testing
Deload/transition: if recovered after week 3, transition to normal strength block; otherwise add week at week 2 intensity or an easy deload week
Additional recovery: sleep hygiene, breathing practices, light walks, reduced evening screen time
Supplements optional: whey protein post-workout, vitamin D if deficient, electrolyte drinks while rebuilding appetite
Reintroduction pacing: drop sets before intensity if RPE rises disproportionately; encourage honest feedback

raw_text:
Goal: Safely restore strength, work capacity and bodyweight over 3 weeks while managing fatigue and avoiding illness relapse. Progress is conservative — focus on movement quality, slightly reduced volumes, auto-regulation, and restoring appetite/weight. Assume client has no medical restrictions beyond recent mild flu.

General rules for the block
- Frequency: 4 gym sessions/week (two upper, two lower) + 1 optional easy conditioning/recovery day.
- Intensity: Start ~60–70% of pre-illness 1RM for main lifts week 1, progress toward ~80–90% by week 3 depending on how he feels. Use RPE and reps-in-reserve (RIR) to auto-regulate; stay 2–3 RIR first week, 1–2 RIR by week 3 on key sets.
- Volume: Reduced compared with typical intermediate cycles. Focus on 2–4 working sets for heavy lifts, moderate assistance volume.
- Tempo & technique: Emphasize controlled eccentrics (2–3s) and full range; pause reps where helpful to rebuild stability.
- Rest & recovery: 2–3 min between heavy sets (3–5 for deadlift variants), 60–90s between accessory sets. Aim for 8–9 hours sleep where possible.
- Nutrition: Aim to regain ~0.5–1 kg/week for first 2 weeks through mild calorie surplus (250–500 kcal/day above maintenance), prioritize protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day, spread evenly across meals, and include calorie-dense snacks if appetite low. Hydration and electrolytes (especially sodium) to support recovery. If weight regained faster, adjust calories to maintenance.
- Monitoring: Check resting HR, and subjective energy/fatigue daily. If persistent elevated resting HR (>8–10 bpm above baseline), or worsening fatigue, reduce intensity/volume and consult physician.
- Warm-up: 8–12 minutes general (bike/row), joint mobility, 2–3 ramp sets before heavy work.
- Cool-down: 5–10 minutes light cardio, foam rolling and breathing practice.

Progression strategy
- Week 1: Re-intro — low-moderate intensity, conservative volume, focus on technique and movement confidence. Main lifts at ~60–70% estimated pre-illness loads or RPE 5–6.
- Week 2: Build — increase intensity to ~70–80% or RPE 6–7, slightly increase sets. Begin heavier singles/doubles on day 3 if recovered.
- Week 3: Peak back toward previous loads — aim for top sets at ~80–90% or RPE 7–8 if feeling recovered. Keep total volume lower than pre-illness week to avoid excessive fatigue. If weight or energy still low, keep conservative.

Three-week plan — 4 sessions/week (Upper A, Lower A, Upper B, Lower B). Day order example: Mon Upper A, Tue Lower A, Thu Upper B, Fri Lower B. Add Sat optional easy conditioning/walk/swim and Sun rest.

Week 1 — Re-intro
- Goal: re-establish movement patterns, build confidence, keep fatigue low.

Session Upper A (Day 1)
1. Warm-up: 8–10 min bike + thoracic mobility, band pull-aparts 2x15.
2. Bench press — ramp to 3 working sets x 6 reps @ ~60% of pre-illness 1RM (pre:100kg → start ~60kg). Keep 2–3 RIR.
3. Seated DB incline press — 3 x 8 @ moderate (RPE 6).
4. Bent-over barbell row or chest-supported row — 3 x 8–10.
5. Face pulls — 3 x 12–15.
6. Farmer carry or suitcase carry — 3 x 40–60s moderate load (grip & conditioning).
7. Core: Dead bug 3 x 10/side controlled.

Session Lower A (Day 2)
1. Warm-up: 8–10 min row, hip mobility, bodyweight squats ramp.
2. Back squat — ramp to 3 x 6 @ ~60% pre-illness (pre:140 → start ~85kg). 2–3 RIR.
3. Romanian deadlift (RDL) — 3 x 8 moderate load (focus hamstring lengthening).
4. Split-squat or Bulgarian split — 3 x 8/leg (bodyweight or light DB).
5. Glute bridge or hip thrust — 3 x 8–10.
6. Calf raises — 3 x 12–15.
7. Conditioning finisher (optional): 10–12 min easy bike intervals (1 min easy / 30s slightly harder) — keep heart rate moderate.

Session Upper B (Day 3 — 48–72h after Day 1)
1. Warm-up: 8–10 min row + scapular push-ups, band warm-up.
2. Close-grip bench or paused bench — 4 x 5 @ ~62–68% (focus triceps and control).
3. Pull-up or lat pulldown — 4 x 6–8 (assisted as needed).
4. Dumbbell shoulder press — 3 x 8.
5. Single-arm DB row — 3 x 8/side.
6. Lateral raises — 3 x 12.
7. Core: Plank 3 x 40–60s.

Session Lower B (Day 4)
1. Warm-up: 8–10 min bike + dynamic hip drills.
2. Deadlift variation — conventional deadlift or trap-bar deadlift — ramp to 3 x 5 @ ~60% pre-illness (pre:170 → start ~100kg). Use conservative set up, 3–5 min rest.
3. Front squat or goblet squat — 3 x 6–8 (lighter, emphasis upright torso).
4. Hamstring curls (machine) — 3 x 10–12.
5. Walking lunges — 3 x 10 steps/leg.
6. Ab wheel or hanging knee raise — 3 x 8–12.

Optional Day 5 (active recovery)
- 30–45 min brisk walk, light bike, mobility and breathing work.

Week 1 Notes:
- Keep sessions brisk but not exhausting. He should feel improved energy over the week; otherwise maintain or reduce intensity.
- Protein target 1.8–2.0 g/kg/day and add 2–3 calorie-dense snacks (nuts, shakes) if intake low.

Week 2 — Build
- Increase intensity and slightly increase top sets while monitoring fatigue.

Session Upper A
1. Warm-up.
2. Bench press — ramp to 4 working sets: 1 x 5 @ ~70% + 3 x 4 @ 72–75% (or RPE 6–7). Last set 1–2 RIR.
3. Incline DB press — 3 x 6–8.
4. Barbell rows — 4 x 6–8 (increase load vs week 1).
5. Face pulls — 3 x 15.
6. Farmer carry — 3 x 60s slightly heavier.
7. Core: Pallof press 3 x 8/side.

Session Lower A
1. Squat — ramp to 4 x 5 @ ~70% (pre-illness 140 → top sets ~98kg). Keep technique focus, 2 RIR.
2. RDL — 3 x 6 heavier than week 1.
3. Bulgarian split squat — 3 x 8/leg heavier DBs.
4. Hip thrust — 3 x 8.
5. Calf raises — 4 x 12.
6. Optional conditioning: 10–15 min low-impact (bike) steady.

Session Upper B
1. Close-grip/paused bench — 4 x 4–5 @ ~72–75%.
2. Pull-ups — 4 x 6 (add small assistance or light weight as needed).
3. Seated DB press — 3 x 6–8 heavier.
4. Chest-supported single-arm row — 3 x 8/side.
5. Lateral raises & rear-delt superset — 3 x 12 each.
6. Core: Plank variations 3 x 45–60s.

Session Lower B
1. Deadlift — ramp to 4 x 4 @ ~70–75% of pre-illness (top sets ~120–130kg). Stop 1–2 reps shy of failure.
2. Front/goblet squat — 3 x 6–8.
3. Hamstring curl — 3 x 8–10 heavier.
4. Walking lunges or step-ups — 3 x 10/leg.
5. Ab wheel/hanging leg raises — 3 x 8–12.

Week 2 Notes:
- If energy is good, you can add a single heavy double or single on day with deadlift at RPE 7–8 for confidence (not maximal).
- Keep nutrition as week 1; increase overall calories if weight not trending up by mid-week.

Week 3 — Return close to pre-illness loads
- Goal: Return to near pre-illness intensities for top work sets while keeping total volume relatively lower than usual to avoid overreaching.

Session Upper A
1. Warm-up.
2. Bench press — work up to 3 sets x 3 reps @ ~80–85% pre-illness (or RPE 7–8). Example top set near 80–85kg if feeling good. Keep 1–2 RIR on final set if fatigue lingers.
3. Incline DB press — 3 x 6.
4. Barbell row — 3 x 5–6 heavier, focus on controlled reps.
5. Face pulls — 3 x 15.
6. Carries — 3 x 60s.
7. Core: Anti-extension work 3 x 8–10.

Session Lower A
1. Squat — work to 3 x 3 @ ~80–85% pre-illness (top sets ~112–119kg). If nervous, reduce by 5–10%.
2. RDL — 3 x 6 heavy but controlled.
3. Bulgarian split — 3 x 6–8 heavier.
4. Hip thrust — 3 x 6–8.
5. Calf raise — 3 x 12–15.

Session Upper B
1. Bench variant (close-grip/paused) — 3 x 3–4 @ ~80% for the variant.
2. Pull-ups or weighted pull-ups — 4 x 4–6 (add weight if recovered).
3. DB shoulder press — 3 x 6.
4. Single-arm row — 3 x 6–8.
5. Delts/upper back accessory — 3 x 12.
6. Core: 3 x 45–60s plank.

Session Lower B
1. Deadlift — work up to 3 x 3 @ ~80–85% of pre-illness (top sets ~136–145kg) only if energy and technique are solid. Otherwise keep at ~75% and focus on form.
2. Front squat/goblet — 3 x 5–6.
3. Hamstring curl — 3 x 8–10.
4. Lunges/step-ups — 3 x 8–10/leg.
5. Core: Hanging leg raises 3 x 8–12.

Week 3 Notes:
- If the client reports persistent fatigue or weight still low, reduce top intensities to ~75% and keep reps slightly higher to rebuild without undue stress.
- Do not push to true PRs in this block — the purpose is reconditioning and returning to baseline with safety.

Deload/transition advice after block
- After week 3, if he’s back near pre-illness weights and energy is normal, transition into a normal 4–8 week strength block with usual volume. If still recovering, add an extra week at the Week 2 intensity or insert an easy deload week (reduced sets and intensity).

Additional recovery and lifestyle recommendations
- Sleep: target 8+ hours and a consistent sleep schedule.
- Stress management: breathing practices, light walks, and reduced evening screen time.
- Supplements (optional): 20–30 g whey protein post-workout if appetite limited, vitamin D if deficient, and electrolyte drinks while rebuilding appetite.
- Reintroduction pacing: Encourage honest feedback — if RPE rises disproportionately, back off volume first (drop sets), then intensity.

Example weekly loads (starting point)
- Bench pre-illness 100kg: Week1 top sets ~60kg x6; Week2 top ~70–75kg x5; Week3 top ~80–85kg x3.
- Squat pre 140kg: Week1 ~85kg x6; Week2 ~98–100kg x5; Week3 ~112–120kg x3.
- Deadlift pre 170kg: Week1 ~100kg x5; Week2 ~120–130kg x4; Week3 ~135–145kg x3 (adjust to how he feels).

Final advice
- Reassess at end of week 3: test 1–3 rep max attempts only if he feels fully recovered, well-rested, and bodyweight and appetite are restored. Otherwise allow another week or two of progressive loading.
- Keep communication daily about sleep, appetite, muscle soreness, and mood so you can adjust loads/volume.

If you want, I can convert this into a printable week-by-week table with exact sets/loads and warm-up prescriptions, or adjust frequency (e.g., 3 days/week) to suit his schedule.
